% Files of the document named like .4ht files, read after a file of the
% same name from TeX's tree: dvipsnam.ltx after
% \usepackage[dvipsnames]{xcolor}, which reads dvipsnam.def, and latin1.ltx
% after \usepackage[latin1]{inputenc}, which reads latin1.def. As in the
% PDF, each file's text is in the page, a named color keeps its value, and
% the degree sign is set as latin1.4ht sets it.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage[dvipsnames]{xcolor}
\input{dvipsnam.ltx}
\usepackage[latin1]{inputenc}
\input{latin1.ltx}
\begin{document}
Dvipsnam: \owndvipsnam

\textcolor{BrickRed}{Brick red text.}

Latin1: \ownlatin

An angle of 30\textdegree.
\end{document}
